# Requirements Document

## Introduction

This document defines the requirements for a **Task Management Platform** that enables teams to organize work into projects, track tasks through completion, collaborate via comments, stay informed through email notifications, and monitor progress through a reporting dashboard.

The system is intentionally scoped to a **handful of services** to keep operational complexity low:

1. **User & Auth Service** — accounts, authentication, authorization, profile management.
2. **Project & Task Service** — projects, tasks, task assignment, status/lifecycle, comments.
3. **Notification Service** — email notifications triggered by platform events.
4. **Reporting Service** — aggregated dashboards and reports across projects and tasks.

These services share a common identity model (user accounts) and communicate via well-defined APIs and/or events. No further service decomposition (e.g., separate comment service, separate search service) is in scope.

---

## 1. User Accounts

### 1.1 User Story
As a new user, I want to create and manage an account, so that I can securely access the platform and be identified as the owner or collaborator of projects and tasks.

### 1.2 Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a visitor submits a registration form with a valid email, password, and display name THEN the system SHALL create a new user account and send a verification email.
2. WHEN a user attempts to register with an email that already exists THEN the system SHALL reject the request with a clear "account already exists" error.
3. WHEN a user submits valid credentials (email + password) THEN the system SHALL authenticate the user and issue a session token (e.g., JWT).
4. WHEN a user submits invalid credentials THEN the system SHALL reject the login and SHALL NOT reveal whether the email or password was incorrect.
5. IF a user's email is not yet verified THEN the system SHALL restrict access to core features until verification is completed.
6. WHEN a user requests a password reset THEN the system SHALL send a time-limited reset link via email.
7. WHEN a user updates their profile (name, avatar, timezone) THEN the system SHALL persist the changes and reflect them across all services that display user identity.
8. WHEN a user deletes their account THEN the system SHALL anonymize or reassign their owned projects/tasks according to a documented retention policy, rather than silently deleting collaborative data.
9. WHERE role-based access is configured, the system SHALL support at least two roles per project (e.g., Owner/Admin and Member) governing who can manage project settings, membership, and delete content.

---

## 2. Projects

### 2.1 User Story
As a team lead, I want to create and organize projects, so that my team has a dedicated space to plan and track related work.

### 2.2 Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an authenticated user creates a project with a name THEN the system SHALL create the project and assign the creator as the Owner.
2. WHEN a project Owner invites another user by email or username THEN the system SHALL add that user as a project Member (pending acceptance if the invitee does not yet have an account).
3. WHEN a project Owner removes a Member THEN the system SHALL revoke that member's access to the project's tasks and comments immediately.
4. WHEN a user who is not a Member of a project attempts to access it THEN the system SHALL deny access and return an authorization error.
5. WHEN a project Owner archives a project THEN the system SHALL hide it from default views while preserving its data for reporting and potential restoration.
6. WHEN a project Owner deletes a project THEN the system SHALL require confirmation and SHALL cascade-remove or archive its tasks and comments per policy.
7. WHERE a project has multiple Members, the system SHALL display a project-level activity/audit trail of key changes (creation, membership changes, deletion).

---

## 3. Tasks

### 3.1 User Story
As a project member, I want to create, assign, and track tasks, so that my team can coordinate and monitor the progress of work.

### 3.2 Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a project Member creates a task with a title within a project THEN the system SHALL create the task in a default status (e.g., "To Do") and associate it with that project.
2. WHEN a task is created or edited THEN the system SHALL allow optional fields: description, assignee, due date, priority, and labels/tags.
3. WHEN a Member assigns a task to a project Member THEN the system SHALL notify the assignee (see Section 4) and display the task in the assignee's task list.
4. WHEN a Member changes a task's status (e.g., To Do → In Progress → Done) THEN the system SHALL record the change with a timestamp and the acting user.
5. IF a task's due date passes without the task being marked complete THEN the system SHALL flag the task as overdue in relevant views and reports.
6. WHEN a Member deletes a task THEN the system SHALL require confirmation and SHALL remove or archive associated comments consistently with the task's fate.
7. WHEN a user filters or sorts tasks (by assignee, status, due date, priority, or label) THEN the system SHALL return results scoped to projects the user is a member of.
8. WHERE tasks support subtasks or checklists, the system SHALL roll up subtask completion into the parent task's displayed progress.

---

## 4. Comments

### 4.1 User Story
As a project member, I want to comment on tasks, so that my team can discuss details, decisions, and blockers in context.

### 4.2 Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a project Member adds a comment to a task THEN the system SHALL persist the comment with author, timestamp, and task association.
2. WHEN a comment includes an @mention of another project Member THEN the system SHALL trigger a notification to the mentioned user (see Section 5).
3. WHEN the comment author edits their own comment THEN the system SHALL update the content and mark it as edited, preserving the original creation timestamp.
4. WHEN the comment author or a project Owner deletes a comment THEN the system SHALL remove it from the task view while retaining an audit record if required by policy.
5. IF a user who is not a project Member attempts to view or post a comment THEN the system SHALL deny the request.
6. WHEN comments are displayed on a task THEN the system SHALL show them in chronological order and support basic text formatting.

---

## 5. Email Notifications

### 5.1 User Story
As a platform user, I want to receive timely email notifications about relevant activity, so that I stay informed without constantly checking the app.

### 5.2 Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a user is assigned a task THEN the system SHALL send an email notification to the assignee summarizing the task and linking to it.
2. WHEN a user is @mentioned in a comment THEN the system SHALL send an email notification to the mentioned user with the comment context.
3. WHEN a task assigned to a user becomes overdue THEN the system SHALL send a reminder email to the assignee (and optionally the project Owner).
4. WHEN a user is invited to a project THEN the system SHALL send an invitation email with a link to accept and join.
5. IF a user has disabled a specific notification category in their preferences THEN the system SHALL NOT send that category of email while still recording the underlying event.
6. WHEN multiple notification-triggering events occur for the same user in a short window THEN the system SHOULD batch or digest them to avoid excessive email volume, per configurable rules.
7. WHEN an email notification fails to send THEN the system SHALL retry according to a defined policy and SHALL log the failure for observability.
8. WHERE a user updates their notification preferences THEN the system SHALL apply the new preferences to all future notification events immediately.

---

## 6. Reporting Dashboard

### 6.1 User Story
As a team lead or stakeholder, I want a reporting dashboard, so that I can understand project health, team workload, and progress trends at a glance.

### 6.2 Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a user with appropriate project access opens the dashboard THEN the system SHALL display summary metrics: total tasks, tasks by status, overdue tasks, and completion rate.
2. WHEN a user selects a specific project THEN the system SHALL scope all dashboard metrics and charts to that project.
3. WHEN a user selects a date range THEN the system SHALL recompute trend charts (e.g., tasks created vs. completed over time) for that range.
4. WHEN a user views workload distribution THEN the system SHALL display task counts grouped by assignee across the selected project(s).
5. IF underlying task or project data changes THEN the system SHALL reflect updated metrics on the dashboard within a defined refresh interval (e.g., near-real-time or on a scheduled batch, per implementation).
6. WHEN a user exports a report THEN the system SHALL generate a downloadable file (e.g., CSV/PDF) reflecting the currently applied filters.
7. WHERE a user lacks access to a project THEN the system SHALL exclude that project's data from any aggregated dashboard the user views.

---

## 7. Cross-Cutting Requirements

### 7.1 Security & Access Control
1. WHEN any service handles a request THEN the system SHALL authenticate the caller via a shared identity mechanism issued by the User & Auth Service.
2. WHEN authorization is evaluated THEN the system SHALL enforce project membership and role checks consistently across the Project & Task Service and Reporting Service.
3. THE system SHALL encrypt data in transit (TLS) and at rest for sensitive fields (e.g., credentials, tokens).

### 7.2 Reliability & Observability
1. WHEN a service-to-service call fails (e.g., Notification Service unreachable) THEN the system SHALL degrade gracefully without blocking core task/project operations.
2. THE system SHALL log key domain events (account creation, project/task changes, notification dispatch) to support auditing and troubleshooting.

### 7.3 Performance & Scalability
1. WHEN a project contains a large number of tasks (e.g., thousands) THEN task list and dashboard queries SHALL remain responsive through pagination, indexing, or pre-aggregation.
2. THE system SHALL be able to scale the Notification Service independently to absorb bursts of email-triggering events without impacting the Project & Task Service.

### 7.4 Data Retention & Compliance
1. WHEN a user or project is deleted THEN the system SHALL follow a documented, consistent retention/deletion policy across all four services.
2. THE system SHALL provide users the ability to export their own data upon request.

---

## 8. Out of Scope

- Real-time chat or video collaboration.
- Third-party integrations (e.g., Slack, GitHub) beyond email notifications.
- Mobile native applications (web-responsive experience only, unless specified later).
- Multi-tenant billing/subscription management.
- Additional microservices beyond the four defined above (e.g., dedicated search, audit, or file-storage services) unless a future revision of this document expands scope.
